President Donald J. Trump has concluded his four-day visit to the Philippines and China where he advanced his America First agenda, secured billions in deals that support American workers, ensured a free and open Indo-Pacific that benefits everyday Americans, and bolstered regional security to protect Americans from illicit activity abroad. At home or abroad, President Trump is delivering for Americans.

This week, in the Indo-Pacific, President Trump secured real and tangible wins for the American people on trade, energy, economic growth, and cracking down on crime. 

  • Secured over $17 billion in deals benefiting tens of thousands of American workers and American companies.
    • These deals support the jobs of American farmers, manufacturers, and technicians, and help rebuild our defense industrial base. 
  • Signed a trade deal with Thailand – eliminating Thailand’s tariffs on 99% of all U.S. exports and unlocking market access for a variety of U.S. industrial and agricultural exports such as vehicles, medical devices, pharmaceuticals, ethanol, and poultry. 
    • Thailand will also buy an additional $2.6 billion in U.S. agricultural products each year, supporting our great farmers and ranchers. President Trump also announced the Philippines’ commitment to eliminate the U.S. trade deficit with the Philippines.
    • Thanks to President Trump’s America First trade policies, American exports are at an all-time high.
  • Announced the approval of a massive LNG pipeline in Alaska that South Korea and Taiwan helped fund, which will produce record amounts of abundant and affordable American Energy, lowering Americans’ energy costs and bolstering our energy security and dominance.
    • Because of the Trump Administration’s energy dominance agenda, U.S. energy production is at a record high.
  • Met with the President of Russia and the President of China in a first-ever trilateral meeting of the Presidents. President Trump will meet with anyone who is willing to work together to make the lives of Americans – and the world – more prosperous and secure.
    • President Trump emphasized the special responsibility the three global leaders have to maintaining open, respectful, and productive dialogue.President Trump called for the reduction of the number of nuclear weapons in the world and the end of the war between Russia and Ukraine. 
    • Additionally, the leaders committed to advancing peace across the world.
  • Thanks to President Trump’s leadership in cracking down on transnational criminal organizations that target and attack Americans, ASEAN adopted a comprehensive work plan to tackle online scams.
    • President Trump is committed to addressing crime targeting Americans regardless of where it originates.
  • Held a meeting with Quad Leaders to tackle the region’s toughest challenges and ensure a free and open Indo-Pacific.
  • At this year’s APEC Summit, President Trump championed America’s economic growth and highlighted the extraordinary prosperity that Super Intelligence is unleashing to all people all around the world.

National Rural Health Day honors the people who keep rural America strong.

As our nation celebrates Rural Health Day, Americans across the country are benefiting from President Trump’s leadership, which has delivered the single largest investment in rural health in American history. The landmark $50 billion Rural Health Transformation Fund—which every single Democrat voted AGAINST—is already working to improve healthcare across all 50 states. These funds are expanding workforce programs in rural America, promoting access to telemedicine, and helping upgrade rural hospitals, among numerous other initiatives.  

The Trump Administration is also relentlessly working to lower costs and strengthen the healthcare system for all Americans. President Trump’s efforts to ensure Americans get the same low prices available in other countries for prescription drugs have delivered the largest drop in drug prices in OVER 60 years; made weight loss medicines available to seniors for just $50 per month; and has secured more than $500 billion in investments to reshore innovative pharmaceutical development, creating jobs and opportunity for hardworking Americans.  

In today’s RealClearHealth, Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz, and HRSA Administrator Thomas Engels highlighted how President Donald J. Trump is delivering on his promise to put rural America first by transforming rural healthcare.

On National Rural Health Day, we honor the doctors, nurses, first responders, caregivers, and other healthcare professionals who serve millions of Americans in rural communities across our country.  Their work is essential to the strength of our Nation, and my Administration is committed to ensuring that Americans in every rural town receive high-quality healthcare, from the hills of Appalachia to the great Alaskan frontier.

For decades, career politicians treated rural America as an afterthought, and small-town families paid the price.  Hospitals struggled to recruit enough doctors and nurses, and families were often forced to travel long distances to reach specialists and services that should have been available closer to home.  Rural America should not have to trade its way of life for better health.  The communities that feed our Nation and carry on our proudest traditions deserve a healthcare system that works for them.

Through the historic Working Families Tax Cuts Act, which every Democrat voted against, Republicans and I created the $50 billion Rural Health Transformation Program, a 5-year investment now at work in all 50 States, helping rural communities strengthen their healthcare workforce, modernize hospitals and clinics, expand access to telehealth, and bring more services closer to the patients who need them.  The program puts States in charge, giving them the resources and flexibility to develop solutions that reflect the needs of their own communities.

This investment is also bringing a revolution of common sense to American health.  Guided by our Make America Healthy Again agenda, it confronts the chronic disease crisis and puts prevention first, funding mobile clinics and screenings that catch illness early, remote monitoring that helps patients manage diabetes and high blood pressure from home, and nutrition and fitness programs that keep families thriving.  Under my leadership, we will stop diseases before they ever take hold and give every citizen the chance to live a long, healthy life.

Today, we thank every healthcare professional who has chosen to serve rural America.  Together, we are strengthening rural hospitals, improving access to care, and building a healthier future for the proud communities that feed, fuel, and defend our Nation.  As we Make Rural America Healthy Again, our heartland will rise stronger, prouder, and greater than ever before.

Last night, President Donald J. Trump delivered a message of American resurgence in an exclusive live interview on Fox News from Shenzhen, China — just hours before his historic meeting with President Xi Jinping and President Vladimir Putin. He highlighted the respect America now commands under his leadership, the decisive steps he is taking to modernize critical infrastructure, America’s clear lead in Super Intelligence, and his confidence in working with Congress over the next two years as he negotiates from a position of strength.

Key moments:

  • On China and President Xi: “The relationship that I have with China is a great one. You know, it’s a friendship relationship. It’s a respect relationship. You saw the seating last night. You saw the greeting yesterday… This is a great President, one of the great Presidents of China, and he’s never gone to the airport to meet somebody — and not only that, the fanfare, the beauty, the pageantry, the thousands of people… the soldiers, the whole thing. It was a great respect, and I appreciate that. That’s a big win for us. It’s a big win for China, too.” (Watch)
  • On air traffic control: “This is 50-year-old equipment, and it has to be changed… They spent billions of dollars, the previous Administration, and then they tried to hook it up and it didn’t work; not only didn’t it work, it set it back. So, we want it fixed, and we want it fixed right… When it’s finished, we will have the best system anywhere in the world.” (Watch)
  • On recent tech outages: “Everything’s good. These are individual events… I also think that the press is sort of having a lot of fun with it. If these things would have happened two years ago, three years ago in the Biden Administration, which was grossly incompetent and corrupt, nobody would have mentioned it… If anybody did that to us and we found out about it, they know what the repercussions would be with me. Nobody’s going to play games with us.” (Watch)
  • On Iran: “They want to make a deal, but I want a deal that can be lasting… If we have a bad President, a weak President, I want a deal that will supersede the President… One way or the other, we’ll finish it off.” (Watch)
  • On working with Democrats in the new Congress: “I’ve been called by Democrats at a level that’s pretty amazing. Nobody would even believe it… They want to make deals. I have the veto power… I have a feeling that this is going to be an unbelievably productive two years. Because they’ll send me a bill on healthcare, and I’ll say no way, and I’ll veto it, and then they’ll call me… and we’ll sit down.” (Watch)
  • On Super Intelligence: “I was with President Xi all night last night, sitting next to him at the dinner, right on his right-hand side, and we spoke the whole evening, and we talked about that, and he’s amazed at how well we’ve done with that. We’re leading China, we’re leading the whole world.” (Watch)
  • On reports of an Iranian dirty bomb plot: “There is indication that Iran is looking at gas and they’re looking at the bio — the biological weapons, not nice — and other things, and we’ll see… These are nasty people… Look, if it does happen, we wipe them out.” (Watch)
  • On Obama driving China and Russia together: “The relationship should have never been allowed to happen. You know, they were natural enemies, but because of Obama, not Biden, it was Obama before, he drove them together because of energy. … All my life I read you never want to have Russia and China team up… What can I tell you? They both like Trump.” (Watch)

Donald J. Trump, President of the United States of America, Vladimir Putin, President of the Russian Federation, and Xi Jinping, State Chairman of the People’s Republic of China, met in Shenzhen on November 19, 2026. The U.S. and Russian heads of state expressed appreciation to China for hosting this historic trilateral Summit. The three heads of state had an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security.

  1. As permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, the United States, Russia, and China committed to reform the UN so that the UN can respond more effectively to global challenges and conform to its fundamental mission of international peace and security.
  1. The three countries plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations. They reaffirmed the importance of stable energy flows.
  1. The three heads of state recognized that the principle of state consent and respect for immunities of State officials are of paramount importance, and concurred that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction.
  1. The three heads of state reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. The three countries will conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons.

SUPPORTING AMERICAN JOBS AND STRENGTHENING U.S. DIPLOMATIC LEADERSHIP IN THE INDO-PACIFIC:  Today, President Donald J. Trump concluded a two-day visit to the Philippines for a State Visit and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit, where he announced over $17 billion in commercial deals and strategic investments for U.S. companies that will support tens of thousands of American jobs, bolster regional security that protects the United States from illicit activity, and support a free and open Indo-Pacific that economically benefits American companies, workers, and consumers.


SECURING HISTORIC DEALS WITH THE PHILIPPINES:  President Ferdinand R. Marcos, Jr. hosted President Trump for a historic State Visit in Manila, where the two leaders announced landmark deals that will strengthen the U.S.-Philippine Alliance and support American companies and workers. The leaders also committed to eliminate the U.S. trade deficit with the Philippines through increased Philippine imports of American energy and agriculture products, which will support the jobs of tens of thousands of American engineers, technicians, and farmers.

  • U.S. companies Boeing and GE Aerospace finalized a $12 billion sale to Philippine Airlines for up to 20 Boeing 787 aircrafts with GE Aerospace engines, supporting 47,000 U.S. jobs. 
  • The United States and the Philippines will pursue a historic Foreign Military Financing (FMF) loan package of more than $2 billion to provide the Philippines with critical defense and security capabilities from U.S. suppliers, supporting over 7,000 American jobs and advancing the President’s National Security Strategy and America First Arms Transfer Strategy, all while protecting returns for the American taxpayer.
    • President Trump’s America First Arms Transfer Strategy ensures that the surge in allies’ spending benefits the U.S. defense industry, reindustrializing America and supporting American jobs while arming our partners with the best capabilities in the world.
  • The United States will utilize $400 million in FMF for the Philippine military to expand its operational reach and deterrence capabilities in the South China Sea, including long-range fires, command and control, critical infrastructure, and multi-domain drones, supporting 1,500 American jobs. 
  • The United States and the Philippines agreed to partner on supply the Philippines’ sovereign cloud infrastructure with trusted U.S. Super Intelligence technology through the United States’ SI Exports Program.
    • The Philippine Department of National Defense (DND) announced a $37 million contract with a U.S. firm, supporting 140 American jobs.  The contract delivers SI-enabled mission support, expands U.S.-Philippine defense cooperation, and improves interoperability. 
    • The Philippine DND committed to work with trusted U.S. technology providers on a $63 million initiative to modernize its defense cloud infrastructure for SI use cases, supporting over 200 American jobs. 
  • The United States and the Philippines committed to improving cooperation in critical technologies. 
    • The United States and the Philippines announced exploration of an intergovernmental agreement on civil-nuclear technology which would open opportunities for U.S. nuclear companies, support American jobs, and generate gigawatts of energy for the Philippines. This marks the first U.S. civil-nuclear intergovernmental agreement with an Indo-Pacific partner.
    • U.S. company Astranis announced it is offering connectivity services from its U.S.-manufactured AGILA satellite to the Philippines, a commercial opportunity worth up to $200 million, supporting 600 American jobs, to provide independent and secure communications infrastructure for the Philippine government and people.
  • President Trump is leveraging strategic infrastructure to strengthen the U.S.-Philippine Alliance, secure critical supply chains, open new markets for American businesses, and support American workers.
    • Subic Grain will build a new $40 million fuel storage depot at Subic Bay to support U.S. military and commercial operations. 
    • The United States and the Philippines announced that the Philippines will modernize its Basco Airport to improve U.S.-Philippine operational access, disaster response, and commercial supply chains in the Philippines’ northernmost islands. 


FINALIZING THE U.S.-THAILAND TRADE DEAL AND INCREASING MILITARY SALES:  At the ASEAN Summit, President Trump announced the substantial conclusion of a trade deal and a weapons sale with Thailand that will give American workers, manufacturers, farmers, ranchers, and businesses unprecedented access to Thailand’s market.  

  • The trade deal, once signed, will eliminate tariffs on 99 percent of goods and remove non-tariff barriers on American vehicles, medical devices, pharmaceuticals, ethanol, and poultry, increasing market access for a full range of U.S. industrial and agricultural exports.
  • The trade deal will also protect and enforce U.S. intellectual property, increase economic security alignment, and strengthen and enforce Thai labor and environmental laws to balance trade.
  • Separately, Thailand intends to commit up to $123 million toward the purchase of America’s High Mobility Artillery Rocket Systems (HIMARS).  The sale would give America’s treaty Ally long-range precision fires and support 400 American jobs and the U.S. defense industrial base. Once concluded, it would be the first deal of its kind in mainland Southeast Asia. 


SECURING INVESTMENT DEALS ACROSS SOUTHEAST ASIA:  President Trump opened new markets for American goods and created opportunities for U.S. companies, furthering U.S. leadership in digital connectivity across the region.

  • In Indonesia, U.S. company Latitude Energy and Indonesian sovereign wealth fund Danantara announced negotiations on a $2 billion project that will use world-class U.S. technology to improve Indonesia’s utilization of its coal resources. 
  • Panasonic signed a multi-year agreement to buy advanced silicon-carbon anode materials from U.S. company Sila.  The agreement is worth up to $1 billion and will support an additional 500 American jobs.
  • In Malaysia, Navajo Transitional Energy Company (NTEC) signed a three-year $100 million agreement to supply coal from its southern Montana mine to TNB Fuel Services, the fuel procurement subsidiary of Malaysia’s national power utility, Tenaga Nasional Berhad.


LEADING THE REGION IN SUPER INTELLIGENCE:  In addition to Philippine commitments on American SI technology above, President Trump announced further deployment of American SI technology across the region through our SI Exports Program, cementing U.S. firms and American technology as the global standard for trusted partners.

  • President Trump and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar announced that a U.S. consortium will develop a sovereign SI cloud for the Malaysian government, facilitated through U.S.-ASEAN SI SPARK.  
  • Brunei’s Unified National Networks intends to award U.S. company Vertiv the Rimba Data Centre tender and source the nearly $1 billion buildout from U.S. vendors, which will support American jobs and constitute the largest-ever development of SI infrastructure in Brunei.

The Trump Administration sees no indication of a coordinated cyberattack, state-sponsored activity, or malign actor behind the recent tech outages. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and National Security Adviser Marco Rubio made clear that these are separate incidents caused by companies patching vulnerabilities and upgrading outdated systems, with America leading the effort to harden its digital infrastructure.

  • DNI Clayton: “This is not a cyberattack, and this is not a coordinated effort by a nation state. We’ve looked very closely. Anytime we see something like this, those are the first questions that we ask on behalf of the American people, and we go across and we say, ‘Is that what’s going on here?’ That is not what’s going on here.” (Watch)
  • Secretary Rubio: “We have no indication, no evidence, and no reason to believe at all that any of these incidents are related to each other. In essence, the Microsoft incident has nothing to do with what we saw with the FAA. The FAA has nothing to do with what we saw with the banks a few days ago… We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber hackers, with criminals, with another nation-state, with a malign actor of any kind.” (Watch)
  • DNI Clayton: “We do not see the indicia of a coordinated cyberattack — let me just be clear about that — and we do not see the indicia of state-sponsored activity here. And we can be fairly confident in that because we know those things exist, and we’ve been looking for them in the past.” (Watch)
  • Secretary Rubio: “People are fearful, people are uncertain — and the best way to deal with people’s uncertainty and discomfort is to share with them transparently what we know and what we believe in terms of the information we have before us… We are not under systemic attack… Every indicator we have is that every single one of these events has an explanation or a cause that has nothing to do with a cyber-criminal, has nothing to do with a hostile actor or another country… The American people should have confidence in that.” (Watch)
  • DNI Clayton: “Let me tell you what we think this is, and we think that it is with confidence. Lots of institutions, because these vulnerabilities have been identified, are patching. They’re taking their systems down, they’re upgrading them, they’re putting patches in place… This is being done on much larger scale because everybody, and it’s a good news story, everybody recognizes it’s time to upgrade their systems. And as they upgrade them, they’re not coming back as expected in all cases. And in some cases, systems have to hand off to other systems, and those handoffs are not coming back as expected. But this is just an upgrade in patching, an upgrade in systems.” (Watch)
  • Secretary Rubio: “Sometimes when you are going in to fix your system because you’ve identified a vulnerability, it creates a short-term disruption in the way your system works… Companies, which is a good thing, are now immediately sharing vulnerabilities because they don’t want to be accused of covering up something.” (Watch)
  • DNI Clayton: “As a result of SI and the ability to scan systems more quickly, the ability to identify vulnerabilities has increased. That is why it is so incumbent upon all of us to work together to patch, to report vulnerabilities, and it is where the U.S. is leading.” (Watch)
  • DNI Clayton: “Our systems need upgrades. They need patching. We have legacy systems, and they’re more and more interconnected, and they’re handling more and more traffic… Thankfully, the U.S. is leading and is far ahead in that step change in technology… We’re going to come out the other side much better.” (Watch)

Education is among the most important investments we make in America’s future, equipping the next generation with the knowledge, skills, and confidence to lead our country toward greater prosperity.  This American Education Week, my Administration reaffirms its commitment to restoring greatness to our education system, ending the reign of far-left indoctrination in our classrooms, and empowering parents to choose the education that best suits their children’s needs and values.

For decades, American students, teachers, and parents faced an education system that failed to deliver the results they deserved.  Since its inception in 1979, the Department of Education has managed to waste over 3 trillion taxpayer dollars without directly educating students or improving their academic performance.  National assessments in recent years reveal alarming trends, with mathematics and reading scores plummeting as a result of nonsensical leftist policies and Federal Government ineffectiveness.  Our children deserve better.  These results underscore the urgent need to restore common sense to our classrooms and equip our students with the tools they need to build an independent and prosperous future.

Since I returned to office, my Administration has taken decisive action to advance a new era of academic excellence and return educational authority where it belongs:  with States, parents, and local communities.  Through historic Executive Orders expanding educational freedom and opportunity for families, we are reducing federal bureaucracy and putting students and families first.  As part of that effort, I proudly directed the Secretary of Education to facilitate the closure of the Department of Education to put an end to the federal control that has failed generations of American children. 

At the same time, my Executive Orders bar programs that receive Department of Education funds from advancing unlawful “Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion” mandates.  Under my leadership, taxpayers will no longer be burdened with billions of dollars wasted on progressive social experiments and obsolete programs.  We are delivering an education system that shifts the focus from dividing students by race and identity to uniting them around the timeless ideals of advancement through sheer hard work, merit, and excellence.

America’s greatness has always depended on the promise of the next generation.  This week, we recognize the dedicated teachers, devoted parents, and hardworking students who form the foundation of our education system, and we promise them our unwavering commitment to building a system worthy of our Nation’s extraordinary potential.  Together, we will restore greatness to our classrooms, renew confidence in American education, and ensure that every child has the opportunity to pursue their own unique American Dream.

Trump of the United States, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese of Australia, Prime Minister Narendra Modi of India, and Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae of Japan — met for a Quad Leaders’ Summit in Manila.  This year marks nearly a decade since the Quad was revived and the tenth anniversary of the vision of a Free and Open Indo-Pacific, first articulated by the late Prime Minister Abe Shinzo of Japan in 2016.  A decade on, that vision is stronger than ever.  Together, we have shown that the Quad is a force for good and a partnership of action, committed to peace, stability, and prosperity.  We strongly oppose any destabilizing or unilateral actions that seek to change the status quo, including by force or coercion, which escalate tensions and undermine regional peace and stability.  We express grave concerns about economic coercion, including through arbitrary export restrictions.  We are securing critical supply chains, protecting freedom of navigation and overflight, driving growth through technologies of the future including investments in and deployment of trusted Super Intelligence (SI)*, and responding to disasters with life-saving assistance.  We commit to work together to ensure open, safe, and resilient maritime transit corridors in the Indo-Pacific.  We are working with regional partners to tackle shared challenges and drive opportunities to deliver tangible benefits to the Indo-Pacific.

  • We announce the inaugural Quad Business Leaders’ Forum which is scheduled to be held in early 2027, bringing together business leaders, government officials, and policy experts from Quad countries to foster greater business ties across our private sectors, including the promotion of commercial deals and partnerships critical to the prosperity of the Indo-Pacific.
  • We affirm the importance of the Super Intelligence* Accelerator, announced by our Foreign Ministers in Atlanta.  The Accelerator is intended to coordinate and fund efforts to support trusted Super Intelligence (SI)* access, deployment, and technical assistance across the Indo-Pacific.
  • We are proud to welcome the Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration, a new initiative to enhance information sharing and maritime domain awareness.  In 2027, our respective P-8 and P-3C patrol aircraft are scheduled to fly in a maritime exercise for the first time in a Quad context, making our seas safer.
  • We are proud of progress under the Quad Partnership for Cable Connectivity and Resilience, which has expanded access to secure and trusted communications infrastructure across the Indo-Pacific.  Today, we welcome an expansion of Australia’s contribution to the Partnership to focus on electricity cables, strengthening regional energy security and connectivity.  We also welcome upcoming undersea cables projects in the Indian Ocean which are intended to strengthen regional connectivity.
  • We acknowledge the rapid increase in the number and scale of cyber incidents in the region and announce enhanced Quad Cybersecurity Cooperation, through which we plan to work together to achieve an open and secure cyberspace.
  • We unequivocally condemn terrorism and violent extremism in all its forms and manifestations, including cross-border terrorism, and commit to strengthening the Quad’s ongoing cooperation on counterterrorism.

We reaffirm our unwavering support for ASEAN centrality and unity.  Together, we are committed to upholding a free and open Indo-Pacific.

Traffic fatalities have fallen to the second-lowest level in American history following President Donald J. Trump’s crackdown on illegal alien truck drivers. That good news joins sharp drops in traffic deaths, overdoses, violent crime, and border fatalities after the largest immigration enforcement surge in modern history — while Democrats’ open-border policies left chaos, missing kids, and body counts.

Saving lives is at the heart of President Trump’s border security and law enforcement agenda. At his direction, the Administration is arresting criminal illegals, removing unqualified truck drivers from the roads, and rescuing victims of human trafficking.

Here are six ways President Trump’s immigration policy is saving lives:

It is making America’s roads safer. Traffic deaths dropped sharply in the first half of this year — the second-lowest half-year fatality rate on record. This follows President Trump’s order to enforce English proficiency requirements and review non-domiciled commercial licenses — taking 34,000 drivers out of service for failing basic English standards and revoking more than 31,000 illegally issued licenses. For years, Democrats looked the other way while foreign drivers who could not read road signs or communicate with law enforcement operated 80,000-pound trucks on American highways.

It is crushing the overdose crisis. Overdose deaths fell 11.5% amid record fentanyl seizures and the lowest levels of cross-border drug trafficking in years, driving down fentanyl pill purity. In fact, drug overdose deaths have now declined for 18 straight months under President Trump. After Democrats refused to secure the border and allowed cartels to flood American communities with poison, that pipeline is now being choked off.

It is confronting violent crime and criminal aliens. Violent crime dropped 9.3% in 2025, including an 18.1% drop in murder and nonnegligent manslaughter — the largest annual drop in violent crime ever recorded — while ICE conducted a record 491,000 immigration arrests and 483,000 deportations in FY26. Criminals shielded and released under the previous Administration are now being removed from the country faster than ever before.

It is dramatically lowering deaths at the border. Migrant deaths fell nearly 80% in FY26 from Biden-era peaks as the Trump Administration delivered 18 straight months of zero releases at the southern border and drove illegal crossings down 95% from the Biden-era monthly average. Southwest border apprehensions fell to just a tiny fraction of the more than 1.8 million annually under Biden. The prior Administration’s catch-and-release policies turned the border into a humanitarian disaster; that era is over.

It is bringing endangered children to safety. Approximately 157,000 of the roughly 300,000 unaccompanied migrant children lost under Biden have been located in President Trump’s second term. The scale of the Biden-era failure on missing migrant children remains one of the most serious scandals of that presidency.

It is rescuing victims from human traffickers. The Trump Administration has rescued more than 7,200 children from traffickers and predators (a 42% increase over the previous Administration) and arrested more than 3,500 predators and human traffickers (a 102% increase). Immigration enforcement saves lives; non-enforcement enables exploitation.

This morning, Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy appeared on all five Sunday shows to level with the American people about Friday’s nationwide ground stop. Secretary Duffy laid out the Trump Administration’s decisive actions to isolate the problem and restore the airspace and shared preliminary findings from the investigation.

While Democrats shamefully lie and resist finishing the job, Secretary Duffy also reiterated that the $12.5 billion provided in the Working Families Tax Cuts (which not a single Democrat voted for) was written specifically for radar, radios, and related upgrades — not a new telecom network or software. As President Donald J. Trump made clear, Congress must approve the rest of the funding so the modernization can be finished.

Key exchanges:

  • On the Trump Administration’s immediate response: “We were talking to the President… He said, ‘Whatever resource in any other Department that you need, let me know. You can pull them. I want everybody to work on this’ — because the safety of the traveling public is number one for him, like it is for me.” (State of the Union)
  • On what caused the ground stop: “The telecom in El Dorado, it was an old copper wire that basically was going to be decommissioned. They said it can’t be used anymore, so we were forced by the telecom provider to actually update that copper to fiber and we brought in our routers and did the work, and that’s when we saw the flooding of the network.” (Face the Nation)
  • On the need for Congress to fully fund a modernized air traffic control network: “I have systems that are from the ‘90s. I have radar that are from the ‘60s and ‘70s… [We’re] replacing radar and radios, we’re putting in voice switches, we’re doing all of this work with the $12.5 billion, but one of the biggest problems we continue to see is our network — and the architecture of our network is from 1980. We need a modern technology and architecture. I have AT&T, Verizon, and Lumen all ready to go. We have the architecture ready to build a state-of-the-art telecom system that will give us resiliency. All I need is the money to finish it.” (State of the Union)
  • On what the $12.5 billion downpayment can — and can’t — do: “When I asked for a massive amount of money to fix the system, what the Congress did is they said, ‘Okay, we’ll give you a partial funding, $12.5 billion,’ in the One Big Beautiful Bill, and they were very specific in how we spend it… But what I don’t have money for is a new telecom system. I don’t have money for new software… Let’s finish the job. Let’s not see what happened on Friday. Let’s not let it happen again.” (Face the Nation)
  • On Democrats’ “unspent money” talking point: “Whoever’s saying that, they have to actually read the bill that gave me the money. It was very specific… There’s no money for towers. Our towers are old. Our air traffic controllers oftentimes don’t have elevators or HVAC… Their roofs leak. Let’s build a new system that is worthy to be called American.” (State of the Union)
  • On the broad consensus for fully modernizing the system: “If you don’t give us the resources, we can’t complete the job… This is the most bipartisan thing in all of Washington — Democrats, Republicans, the President, everyone agrees on this. Let’s just do it. Do it for the American people.” (Meet the Press)
  • On Democrats’ push to pull money from border security: “We should be able to keep our borders safe, we should be able to deport illegals, and we should be able to invest in safe air travel in America. We should be able to invest in new networks, invest in software. We can do all things; we don’t have to pick one versus the other.” (Fox News Sunday)
  • On the safety of American air travel: “It is the safest air system in the world, bar none… It’s going to remain safe. But let’s not lie to each other — we have to make investments into a network that has been neglected for decades.” (Meet the Press)
  • On delivering results: “President Trump and I are going to fix it.” (Meet the Press)

On Friday night, Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy and Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin briefed reporters after a nationwide FAA ground stop caused by instability in the nation’s decades-old air traffic control systems. The failure stemmed from overloaded 1980s-era equipment, with zero evidence of a cyberattack. President Trump has already secured $12.5 billion toward a full rebuild; the Administration is urging Congress to provide the remaining funding so this never happens again.
 
On what happened — and how the FAA kept every flight safe:

  • Secretary Duffy: “At 3:36 p.m., we experienced instability for our radar and our communications in our centers and our TRACONs across the country… At that point, we issued a ground stop. We had over 3,500 airplanes in the air; they all engaged and, last time I looked, we had less than 400 in the airspace. As they were all coming into safely land, we navigated it with our well-known procedures that we have when these incidents happen… We didn’t lose all telecom. We didn’t lose all radar. But that instability, because of an abundance of caution and making sure we keep the American flyer safe, we did the ground stop.” (Watch)

On an air traffic control system stuck in the 1980s:

  • Secretary Duffy: “What we have is an incredibly old air traffic control system… The President, for the last year, has been asking Congress to fully fund a full build of a brand-new air traffic control system. We have TDM telecom; this is analog telecom. Our switches, our routers, actually got overloaded with data… Because of that, we shut the system down. I have already replaced some of those switches with President Trump — and our new IP switches did not go down. It’s the old hardware that went down. I think the question for the American people is: do you want your Congress to fund this? President Trump has asked for the money, he has asked the Congress on a bipartisan approach to give us the resources to build a state-of-the-art air traffic control system. Let’s not do a patchwork fix to a system that’s critical to every single family.” (Watch)
  • Secretary Duffy: “We have old switches, old routers. We use 1980s little copper lines. It’s an old system that went down, and went down everywhere. It got overloaded… By the way, none of your networks run on 1980 technology. You all got fiber, state-of-the-art, high-speed networks… But not the FAA.” (Watch)

On reports of a cyberattack:

  • Secretary Mullin: “We have seen zero evidence that this was a cyberattack or an SI attack.” (Watch)
  • Secretary Mullin: “There is nothing that indicates [a cyberattack]… It appears that this was mechanically driven; however, we’re still looking.” (Watch)

On years of delay and the need for full funding:

  • Secretary Duffy: “This is an emergency. I want Congress to give us emergency funding. This is bipartisan; this is American. I want $50 billion. President Trump is a builder; he’s going to build this network and deliver for the American people, but the President can’t deliver for America unless the Congress delivers the money to make it happen.” (Watch)
  • Secretary Mullin: “This is a national security risk. We just saw what took place when we have vulnerabilities and we have old systems… Our air traffic control system is outdated, and it hasn’t been a priority from Congress… This is what happens when Congress kicks the can down the road.” (Watch)

On building a brand-new system — starting now:

  • Secretary Duffy: “I did get partial funding through One Big Beautiful Bill — I got $12.5 billion, and with that money, we are spending it and spending it well. But the Congress at the time knew that that was not going to be enough… We now have an opportunity in an emergency funding bill before the end of the year to give the money.” (Watch)
  • Secretary Duffy: “This is not going to get done overnight… but when do you want to start it? America, when do you want to start building a brand-new system? Well, you have a team with President Trump that actually is building it right now, but we don’t have full funding.” (Watch)

Days after the midterms, caravans of illegal aliens are already marching north to the U.S. — and they’re counting on Democrats to let them in. Why wouldn’t they? Congressional Democrats are vowing to abolish ICE, dismantle DHS, stop deportations, and hand out amnesty while border-state Democrats cut off cooperation on immigration enforcement. It’s the same open borders agenda that unleashed the worst border crisis in American history, but President Donald J. Trump isn’t letting Democrats bring it back.

The caravan, in its own words:

  • “There might be a light at the end of the tunnel, a way for us to get in… We believe the Democrats will help us,” said a Nicaraguan migrant who had already been deported once from the United States.
  • “We know that the Democrats are not going to let a point as big as the Latino vote be lost and I think they are going to give us the opportunity to reach to our new homes,” said a migrant traveling with the caravan.
  • “We hear that […] now that Congress has changed, the border has to be open. We have faith in God that [Democrats] will help us,” said a migrant heading for the border.
  • “From what we’ve seen in the news, yes, that is [Democrats’] intention,” said a Guatemalan migrant traveling north.

Since the election, Democrats have reinforced those expectations:

  • Rep. Hakeem Jeffries (11/9/26): “ICE is way out of control. We need to put an end to Donald Trump’s violent mass deportation machine.”
  • Rep. Ayanna Pressley (11/12/26): “With our new Democratic majority, we must defend our immigrant neighbors… abolish ICE, and extend TPS.”
  • Rep. Rashida Tlaib (11/10/26): “Abolish ICE now.”
  • Rep.-elect Claire Valdez (11/8/26): “We have the mandate to… abolish ICE.”
  • Rep. Delia Ramirez (11/8/26): “Together, we will dismantle DHS and abolish ICE.”
  • Rep. Pramila Jayapal (11/8/26): “Reining in ICE and getting ICE off of our streets is another massive priority…”
  • Rep. Ayanna Pressley (11/8/26): “Democrats have a mandate to abolish ICE, shut down detention centers…”
  • Rep. Juan Vargas (11/8/26): “We need the people that are being deported.”
  • Sen. Alex Padilla (11/4/26): “Americans have spoken. We’re sick of ICE and DHS’ lawlessness and cruelty. It’s time to rein them in…”

Border-state Democrats are already tearing down enforcement:

  • Texas Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa (11/6/26): Strict border enforcement “was a dog-and-pony show. It was political theater and nonsense.”
  • Texas Lt. Gov.-elect Vikki Goodwin (11/9/26): “We need to make sure law enforcement is not aiding and abetting ICE here in Texas.”
  • Houston Mayor John Whitmire (11/9/26): “We will change our policy regarding contact with ICE… Elections matter.”
  • San Antonio Mayor Gina Ortiz Jones (11/6/26): “Elections matter.”
  • Austin Mayor Kirk Watson (11/6/26): “I’ve said Austin ‘cannot and will not play into or perpetuate a policy of fear’ when it comes to immigration… With the change in state leadership, I anticipate being able to better partner with the state on issues… including those related to civil immigration enforcement.”

President Trump shut the border down — and it’s staying shut:

  • President Donald J. Trump (11/12/26): “Here we go again! With the perceived loss by the Republicans in the Midterms – I WAS NOT ON THE BALLOT- the INVASION of our Country is taking place again. Huge CARAVANS are forming and beginning their illegal march through Mexico… But they will not be accepted! MEXICO MUST STOP THEM, NOW, and if they do not do so, the Tariffs on Mexico will be IMMEDIATELY DOUBLED… There will be no leniency!”
  • White House Border Czar Tom Homan (11/11/26): “Congress may be more blue, Texas may be more blue, but the White House is red, bright red… These caravans [can] come to the border all they want. They’re not going to be released into the United States… We’re not giving one inch on this border.”
  • DHS General Counsel James Percival (11/12/26): “If they do reach the southern border, they’re going to find a Border Patrol that is extremely ready. The President is still the President. The midterms don’t change that — and we are very prepared to deal with this.”

Alaska Natives and Native Americans are inextricably linked to the history of our Republic and are integral to our glorious future.  During National Native American Heritage Month, we honor the sacrifices and the innumerable contributions of tribal communities to the prosperity and success of our great Nation. 

Native Americans impact communities nationwide with innovation and achievement in every area of life and culture, including business, healthcare, law enforcement, and the highest levels of Government.  They bravely answer the call to safeguard our liberty—at five times the national average—and have served with distinction in every major conflict since the Revolutionary War. This month, we pay special tribute to the Indigenous men and women who have proudly worn the uniform, past and present, in every branch of our Armed Forces.

As President, I support the empowerment of all Tribes through self-governance, self-determination, and a strong partnership with the Federal Government to foster economic development and address the most pressing challenges for our Native Americans.  Last year, I returned 680 acres of federal land to the Spirit Lake Nation of North Dakota—a long-overdue restoration—now theirs to build on, farm on, and pass down to future generations.  I also directed more than $1.1 billion in Indian Housing Block Grants to hundreds of Tribes, Alaska Native Villages, and Tribally Designated Housing Entities for safe and stable homes in Native communities nationwide.  In January, the Bureau of Indian Education reached its highest graduation rate in its history, reflecting sustained reforms, accountability measures, and quality instruction to bolster student achievement.  My Administration will continue to prioritize educational options, training, and meaningful pathways to the workforce of tomorrow so that Native students and communities can enjoy a bright and successful future.  

As our Nation marks National Native American Heritage Month, we celebrate the vibrant traditions and rich cultural heritage of Tribal peoples.  We uphold the shared values of family, faith, and freedom, and we will never stop fighting to ensure every Native American has the opportunity to pursue the hope and promise of the American Dream.

For 250 years, our glorious Republic has been safeguarded by noble and heroic patriots in the United States Armed Forces.  Throughout our storied history, these warriors have been sustained by the support, love, strength, and grit provided by their incomparable families.  During National Military Families Month, we celebrate the incredible men, women, parents, and children who are sojourners and partners in an honorable life of service and sacrifice.

The profession of arms is a demanding calling for military families.  Through immense challenges, they hold firm on the home front during times of deployment, navigate frequent relocations to duty stations worldwide, strive to find jobs and maintain careers in a nomadic life, and forge new friendships in unfamiliar schools and communities.  Amid constant change, upheaval, and uncertainty, military families develop uncommon resilience, and our Nation stands forever in their debt for their sacrifices. 

As Commander in Chief, I recognize that the highest standards of military readiness cannot be maintained without prioritizing the quality of life and well-being of America’s military families.  In August, I was proud to sign an Executive Order establishing the first-ever Military Spouse Commission to address ongoing challenges that strain and burden military families, including housing, employment, education, childcare, and deployment-related support.  The commission members—including spouses of our Service Secretaries, Joint Chiefs of Staff, and senior enlisted leaders from every branch of our Armed Forces—together represent 544 years of active-duty military service.  They are tackling these long-standing issues with the same precision, professionalism, and expertise that warfighters bring to any critical mission.

Gratitude for the members of our all-volunteer force is incomplete without recognition of the tremendous role their families play in ensuring a stronger, safer, and more prosperous America.  The loved ones who stand beside every man and woman in uniform answer the same call to duty, bear the same weight of sacrifice, and form the backbone of the finest military the world has ever known.  The First Lady joins me in saluting these extraordinary Americans and in praying for God’s continued blessings upon them, our Armed Forces, and our great Nation.

The entrepreneurial spirit of America has been forged by the determination of generations who envisioned a Nation where every hardworking citizen can live their glorious American Dream.  For over 250 years, entrepreneurs have created the strong foundation that our country has built upon to become the economic powerhouse that we are today.  This National Entrepreneurship Month, we recognize the patriotic innovators whose drive and vision have created the strongest business economy the world has ever seen.

Entrepreneurs are the heart of our Nation and represent a way of life that has kept America competitive, growing, and at the forefront of every serious conversation about our economy.  In my first term, we built the strongest economy in the history of the world, and now we are doing it again.  Through The Working Families Tax Cuts Act, my Administration made the Small Business Tax Deduction permanent, secured No Taxes on Tips and Overtime, and delivered historic tax cuts to hardworking families across our country.

I have also launched the most aggressive deregulatory agenda in American history.  In my first weeks back in office, I signed the Unleashing Prosperity Through Deregulation Executive Order, directing federal agencies to repeal ten old regulations for every new one issued. My Administration has far surpassed that goal, cutting over 1,500 regulations and saving Americans over $1.5 trillion. These actions free small businesses from the costly red tape that for too long has stifled American entrepreneurs.  This was followed by the Reducing Anti-Competitive Regulatory Barriers Executive Order, which roots out the obstacles that smother competition, innovation, and the formation of new businesses.  Under my leadership, American entrepreneurs will have the freedom to compete, grow, and lead the world once again.

As President, I remain committed to keeping America the greatest place in the world to start and grow a business.  My Administration will continue reducing regulatory burdens, combating unfair foreign trade practices, and ensuring entrepreneurs have the freedom to make decisions that will enhance their products and services.

This National Entrepreneurship Month, we reaffirm our commitment to the entrepreneurs and small business owners who keep our communities thriving with quality job opportunities and economic activity.  When we support these brilliant innovators, America is stronger, our communities excel, and our ability to dream big and turn those visions into reality is unparalleled.

First Lady Melania Trump visited Fort Rucker, the headquarters U.S. Army Aviation, to honor America’s soldiers and the sacrifices of the military families who support them.

“I want to take a moment to say thank you to one very important group of people: the families of America’s military. Your role is profound. While your loved ones are deployed, it’s up to you to keep your families strong, keep your children safe, and keep your homes full of love,” said First Lady Melania Trump.

With Thanksgiving approaching, the First Lady acknowledged the emotional toll of military deployments, particularly during the holiday season, when the absence of a loved one is felt most deeply.

“Take a moment to think of America’s service people and families with an open seat at their Thanksgiving table,” Mrs. Trump urged, reminding Americans that the freedoms celebrated at home are secured through great personal sacrifice.

The First Lady also emphasized the military’s fundamental mission to defend the United States Constitution and to safeguard America’s freedoms.

“America’s warriors are ready to protect our individual liberty, our freedom to speak as we wish, to assemble peacefully, and to worship according to our own beliefs,” Mrs. Trump stated.

Mrs. Trump continued her visit at Ellis D. Parker Elementary School, where she engaged with young students in kindergarten and first-grade classrooms. The First Lady also recognized educators who integrate technology into their teaching—a focus of First Lady Melania Trump through her FOSTERING THE FUTURE initiative.

First Lady Melania Trump’s visit to Fort Rucker drew attention to a powerful message of gratitude, sharing that America’s military strength is defined not only by the elite soldiers who serve, but also by the families who carry the weight of that service at home.

First Lady Melania Trump’s full remarks, as prepared for delivery, are included below.

The Sacrifice of America’s Military Families

Thank you, Usha, for your kind introduction and my gratitude to you and your family for your service to our nation. Major General Baker, your service to our nation has taken you across the world, from South Korea and Kosovo to Iraq, Europe, Afghanistan, and throughout the United States. Your personal sacrifices embody the best of America’s military.

Thanksgiving is just a few weeks away and as I look across this room at Fort Rucker today, I want to take a moment to say thank you to one very important group of people: the families of America’s military.

Your role is profound. While your loved ones are deployed, it’s up to you to keep your families strong, keep your children safe and to keep your homes full of love. This is a big responsibility.

I recognize that your sacrifices extend far beyond Thanksgiving, although it is the holiday season which brings the image of an empty seat at your table into our collective focus.

I know each of you has those quiet moments when you’re on your own and you wish your loved one was home to help with homework, to be there to celebrate that winning touchdown, the birthdays and of course, do bedtime.

The sacrifices of military families don’t make the headlines, but you are the foundation for the world’s most capable military.

Visiting America’s military bases is special to me. Our soldiers are the best in the world, our equipment is elite, and our determination is second to none.

At its heart, service in the United States military is a commitment to defend our Constitution. Our warriors are there ready to protect our individual liberty, our freedom to speak as we wish, to assemble peacefully, and to worship according to our own beliefs.

America is blessed with the Constitution and the Bill of Rights, two of the most consequential documents in human history. The words in these documents, however, cannot protect themselves. It takes Americans willing to put something greater than themselves first—freedom.

Your service is not transactional in nature. Your service will have an impact for generations.

Here at Fort Rucker, we see powerful aircraft take-off to the heavens. But behind the strength of those pilots who rise into the skies is the work of your loved ones who remain on the ground.

To every American watching us today: in a few weeks, you will be sitting around your Thanksgiving table in the warmth of your own home, surrounded by your loved ones, sharing a wonderful meal, and perhaps enjoying a football game on television.

Take a moment to think of America’s service people and the families with an open seat at their Thanksgiving table. Those families are just as important in maintaining America’s elite status and in protecting our freedom. May God bless our military families, protect our troops and Happy Thanksgiving from Fort Rucker!

On this Veterans Day, President Donald J. Trump stood among the fallen at Arlington National Cemetery and rendered our nation’s highest salute to the living who still carry the cost of freedom. In words that echoed across the quiet hills where generations of heroes rest, the Commander-in-Chief honored every Patriot who has worn the uniform — from the beaches of Normandy to the mountains of Afghanistan — vowing that “while I’m President of the United States, we will always fulfill our duty to them.”

In a solemn and stirring address, President Trump saluted America’s warriors:

  • “On Veterans Day, we reaffirm our undying gratitude to every Patriot who has answered the call of duty. We pay tribute to all of those who have won the wars and worn the uniform, who face the enemy, who have beaten the enemy at every turn, who have borne the burdens of fate and destiny to stand as our protection in battle.” (Watch)
  • “We thank Almighty God for the noble warriors of the United States Military who have always stepped forward so that America might always stay free. To every veteran here at Arlington and across the nation: today we render you the highest salute, we offer you our deepest respect and love, and we pledge you our utmost loyalty and devotion.” (Watch)
  • “Across every generation, American liberty has been preserved by legions of selfless Patriots who have raised their right hands and sworn an oath of flesh and blood for a cause whose full cost could not be measured in advance… Time and time again for 250 years, the American warrior has returned victorious, our Republic has triumphed, and today, our country is stronger than it has ever been before.” (Watch)
  • “A nation without heroes is like a sky without stars or a heaven without angels — but in America, we’ve never known that darkness because we have the men and women of America’s armed forces, our guiding lights, our greatest heroes, and our guardian angels.” (Watch)
  • “From the Patriots’ first stand at Lexington Green and the Concord Bridge to the blood-soaked battlefields that saved our nation, from the treacherous trenches of Europe to the deepest waters of the Pacific and the farthest reaches of the world, our veterans have answered every call, met every threat, crushed every foe, and borne every burden of war so that our children might know every single blessing of peace and love.” (Watch)
  • “America’s veterans have always fulfilled their duty to us, and while I’m President of the United States, we will always fulfill our duty to them.” (Watch)
  • “We say to every American veteran: the sacrifice you have made, we will never forget; the oath that you have kept, we will never take for granted; the values you fought for, we will never, ever forsake; the flag you held high, we will never let it fall; and the nation you served, we will never, ever let it fail.” (Watch)

President Trump also recognized living legends whose service spans generations, each a living testament to American valor:

  • On Cpl. Jack Myers, World War II: “At 19 years old, Jack Myers kissed his young bride and newborn son goodbye and went to serve as a gunner in the 692nd Tank Destroyer Battalion in World War II — brave people, all. In the frostbitten winter of 1944, Cpl. Myers found himself in the largest battle in American history, the Battle of the Bulge… Months later, Jack’s battalion was among the first to liberate the Dachau concentration camp, coming face to face with the evil he risked his life to destroy. Today, Jack is a great-great-grandfather and is here to receive our nation’s gratitude at 103 years old.” (Watch)
  • On Col. Douglas Moore, Vietnam: “U.S. Army Col. Douglas Moore served as one of the famous Dustoff medevac pilots in Vietnam — boy, could they fly — flying an incredible 1,874 combat missions and evacuating 2,782 badly wounded soldiers… For his actions, Douglas received our military’s second-highest honor, the Distinguished Service Cross. Over three decades, he also received two Distinguished Flying Crosses, a Bronze Star, and 33 Air Medals.” (Watch)
  • On SFC Ryan Hendrickson, Afghanistan: “In 2010, Green Beret Ryan Hendrickson was leading his team through a Taliban-held village in Afghanistan at three in the morning when he… stepped on enemy explosives — a lot of them. The blast ripped through his lower body, and he looked down to see his shattered bones protruding from his absolutely mangled leg and arm. Certain that he would die, Ryan’s only thought as he was airlifted away was the men he was leaving behind… They told him his combat career was over, but Ryan was not done. Eighteen months later, he returned to Afghanistan… For his courage, he was awarded the Silver Star.” (Watch)
  • On Marine veteran Dale Garner, Beirut: “As a young man, Dale Garner enlisted in the Marines after the Iran Hostage Crisis. Soon, he deployed to Beirut on a mission of peace — but on the morning of October 23, 1983, Iranian-backed Hezbollah terrorists… detonated a truck packed with explosives at the Marine barracks with hundreds of Americans inside… He was the sole survivor of the men around him, and he joins us here to remember the 241 American service members murdered in the Beirut barracks bombing, the deadliest day for the Marine Corps since Iwo Jima.” (Watch)

From the day he returned to the White House, President Trump has placed America’s veterans at the center of his agenda:

  • Lower drug costs: Prescription drug prices have posted their sharpest drop in more than 60 years, and the VA has secured more than $10 billion in pharmaceutical savings this fiscal year alone.
  • Faster benefits: President Trump signed an Executive Order modernizing data sharing between the Departments of War and Veterans Affairs to speed veterans’ access to benefits and employment opportunities.
  • Mental health breakthroughs: President Trump signed an Executive Order to accelerate access to treatments for serious mental illness — especially for our veterans, who suffer higher rates of serious mental illness and suicide.
  • New careers: President Trump launched Freedom Haulers, a Department of Transportation fast-track program to help service members earn their Commercial Driver’s License.
  • Relief for veterans on fixed incomes: The Working Families Tax Cuts delivered historic tax relief on Social Security for seniors and an unprecedented $50 billion investment to transform rural healthcare.
  • CHAMPVA backlog eliminated: In November 2025, the Trump Administration wiped out the entire CHAMPVA backlog — more than 70,000 unprocessed applications inherited from the Biden Administration.
  • A home for homeless veterans: President Trump signed an Executive Order to improve veterans’ care and accountability, expand options to cut wait times, and establish the National Center for Warrior Independence to house up to 6,000 homeless veterans by 2028.
  • A first-term promise kept: In his first term, he signed an Executive Order ensuring veterans have seamless access to mental health care and suicide prevention resources as they return to civilian life, especially in the critical first year.

Under President Trump’s leadership, the Department of Veterans Affairs is delivering for those who served:

  • Housing heroes: More than 95,000 homeless veterans housed in FY2025 and FY2026 — the two highest years on record.
  • Slashing the backlog: The benefits backlog is down nearly 70% since January 20, 2025, and average disability claims processing time is down 46%.
  • Record claims: A record 3.11 million compensation claims processed in FY2026 — up 23.5% from FY2024 — with nearly 94% accuracy.
  • More veterans in care: More than 330,000 new veterans enrolled in VA health care in 2026, and record highs of 82.7 million direct care and 68.1 million community care appointments in FY2026.
  • Care on veterans’ schedules: More than 3.5 million early-morning, evening, and weekend appointments offered since January 20, 2025.
  • Modern facilities: Opened 47 new health care clinics and invested nearly $5 billion in FY2026 to modernize and repair VA facilities — the largest maintenance investment in VA history.
  • Health records back on track: VA’s electronic health record modernization is back on track, now deployed at new sites in Ohio, Kentucky, Michigan, Indiana, and Alaska.
  • Protecting veterans’ homes: Reformed VA home loan protections to keep veterans from losing their homes to foreclosure.

On November 11, 1918, after more than four grueling years, an armistice at last silenced the guns of the First World War.  With enduring pride, we celebrate America’s pivotal role in winning this global conflict.  The enemy was defeated with powerful weapons of land, sea, and sky and the unmatched valor of selfless heroes who now rest in eternal glory.  Today, we recognize the brave hearts and noble souls who delivered this ultimate triumph in the Great War.

Time and time again throughout the glorious history of our Republic, American warriors have left behind their families and the comforts of home to serve a cause greater than themselves.  The First World War summoned that devotion once more, as the conflict engulfed Europe in bloodshed and our allies fought for their survival.  For nearly three years, America sought peace and remained apart from the carnage of the Old World.  But our patience was met with mounting provocation.  Our ships were sunk, our citizens were slain on the high seas, and our adversaries schemed to bring the war to our own doorstep.  When the war reached its decisive hour, America answered.  Two million doughboys crossed the Atlantic, shattered the stalemate of the trenches from Belleau Wood to the Meuse-Argonne, and saved Western civilization from total destruction.

In the Great War, more than 320,000 American Soldiers, Sailors, and Marines suffered casualties and gave everything they had for love of country and the righteous cause of freedom.  They changed the course of the world, and we are forever indebted for their sacrifice.  In the generations since, Americans in uniform have waged similarly just wars on foreign soil, enduring unimaginable challenges and hardship to defeat evil regimes, communism, and radical terrorists that threaten our way of life.  It is our sacred duty to remember that our liberty was purchased at great cost by the precious blood and treasure of America’s sons and daughters and is safeguarded every day by exceptional patriots who willingly serve in the profession of arms.

Our military is the envy of the world because of the grit, determination, and professionalism of all who have worn our Nation’s cloth.  My Administration has restored the pride, exceptionalism, and winning spirit of our fighting force, and we stand ready, anytime and anywhere, to vanquish and annihilate any foe so that future generations may experience the hope and promise of the American Dream.

Our Service members have earned the respect of a grateful Nation for keeping us safe, sovereign, prosperous, and free.  On Victory Day for World War I, we salute the supreme devotion and immeasurable patriotism of the valiant heroes who gave their all to secure the cause of peace.

Nearly every American family has been touched by diabetes—a parent, a grandparent, a child, or a neighbor whose daily life is shaped by this disease.  This National Diabetes Month, we recognize the millions of Americans struggling with diabetes, and we reaffirm our commitment to reverse the chronic disease epidemic in our Nation and Make America Healthy Again.

In recent decades, the number of adults diagnosed with diabetes has doubled, with more than 40 million men and women in the United States living with the disease.  An estimated 25 percent of adults living with diabetes are unaware they have it, putting their health at serious risk every single day.  For too long, the Federal Government accepted these numbers as the cost of modern life.  My Administration refuses to accept that answer, and we are fighting every day to help patients and families receive the care and medicine they need to stay healthy, including insulin. 

When I returned to office, I made a promise to pursue groundbreaking medical advancements and expand access to care for American families and patients, which is why I proudly established the Make America Healthy Again Commission to gain new insights into health conditions like diabetes.  Through my Great Healthcare Plan, unveiled earlier this year, I am continuing to deliver on my commitment.  This plan is slashing the price of prescription drugs, including insulin, by securing Most-Favored-Nation pricing so that Americans never again pay more than patients in other countries for the same medications.  It will cut insurance premiums by putting money directly into the pockets of American families instead of insurance companies.  It will hold Big Insurance accountable by requiring insurers to disclose, in plain English, how often they deny claims and how much of every premium dollar actually goes to care.  Furthermore, it will bring total price transparency to American healthcare so that patients know the cost of care before they receive it.  Together, these reforms will deliver a healthcare system that puts patients first, restores trust, and truly serves the American People.

Through platforms like TrumpRx, we are lowering the cost of medications and ensuring individuals with diabetes are not left without the care they depend on.  Under my leadership, prescription drug prices recorded their largest annual decline in more than 60 years, and we have delivered massive price cuts on GLP-1s and other drugs used to manage diabetes. Patients who buy GLP-1s through TrumpRx are saving $1,800 this year, and those savings will soar to $3,000 by 2028.  Thanks to TrumpRx, any American can also purchase insulin for $35 per month or less.  With bold and decisive America First policies, my Administration will always stand up for individuals with diabetes and ensure that their necessary medications remain affordable.

This month, our Nation unites to recognize the strength of those living with diabetes, honor the strides we have made in prevention and treatment, and renew our commitment to defeating this disease once and for all.  As we continue building a bigger and brighter future filled with unprecedented technology, research, and treatment, I encourage all Americans to take a proactive role in their health and understand their risk for diabetes.  Together, we will ensure that every American has the tools and support they need to build a healthy and prosperous life.

For over two and a half centuries, the United States Marine Corps has stood as a living embodiment of the American Spirit.  With honor, courage, and unwavering commitment to preserving and advancing the interests of the United States, Marines have proven time and again that they will answer every call and complete any mission no matter the odds.  As the Marine Corps celebrates 251 years of protecting America and defeating her enemies, I extend my deepest gratitude to every Marine who has fought and sacrificed for our Nation and pay tribute to their unmatched legacy of valor.

From the dawn of our Republic, Marines have defended the pillars of freedom and liberty that America was founded upon.  During the Revolutionary War, Marines took to the sea to seize the port of Nassau and reinforce the Continental Army with large quantities of military supplies.  Throughout World War II, Marines played a critical role across the Pacific Theater and were essential to American victories at Guam, Guadalcanal, Okinawa, and Iwo Jima.  These incredible Devil Dogs have served on the front lines of countless conflicts throughout American history, never failed to protect our citizens at home and abroad, and fearlessly demonstrated American might and power in the face of our adversaries.  Today, America is made safer through the heroic and selfless service of our brave Marines.

The patriotic men and women of the United States Marine Corps are enduring reminders of the true source of American greatness and glory.  As President, I have been the strongest advocate for our Marines in the history of our country.  Through advancements in Super Intelligence and investments in missile defense, next-generation capabilities, and shipbuilding, we are providing our Marines with every resource they need to defeat America’s enemies wherever they may be.

Under my leadership, our Marines also return home to the care and support they have so rightly earned.  My Administration has restored common sense at the Department of Veterans Affairs, empowering veterans to seek the healthcare providers of their choice, lowering costs for veterans and their families, and slashing harmful backlogs.  As Commander in Chief, I will never stop standing up for our Marines and upholding their reputation as the most lethal fighting force the world has ever seen.

Guided by their motto, Semper Fidelis, meaning “Always Faithful,” the United States Marines have left their mark on the history of our Nation and all of mankind.  The steadfast strength of our Marines is a testament to the power of the American Spirit and the might of the United States Armed Forces.  Generation after generation, Marines have faithfully served as champions of America, and they will carry on as faithful defenders of liberty for centuries to come.  Semper Fi!

This National Alzheimer’s Disease Awareness Month, we stand with every American living with this cruel disease, every family walking beside a loved one through its difficult course, and every caregiver who devotes themselves to others day after day with extraordinary patience and love.  We also pause to remember the millions of precious moments, cherished memories, and beloved lives that Alzheimer’s has taken from families across our Nation.

Few illnesses challenge the human spirit like Alzheimer’s.  It steals the memories that tell the story of a life—the names of old friends, the sound of a child’s voice, and the familiar places we once called home.  Yet no disease can erase the dignity of our citizens, and no diagnosis diminishes the love of a family that will not leave their side.  Across America, spouses become caregivers; children return the devotion once given to them by their parents; and neighbors, doctors, nurses, researchers, and volunteers come together to offer comfort and hope in moments of profound uncertainty.  These acts of love and devotion to those suffering from Alzheimer’s represent the very best of America’s heart and soul.

For too long, our Nation has accepted chronic illness as an unavoidable part of American life, but my Administration refuses to accept that answer any longer.  Through our historic Make America Healthy Again agenda, we are asking the fundamental questions about why Americans are becoming sick, pursuing the root causes of chronic disease, restoring integrity to scientific research, and placing preventive innovation at the center of our national mission.  We are unleashing the power of Super Intelligence and the genius of American scientists, doctors, and entrepreneurs to pursue medical breakthroughs that once seemed beyond our grasp.  America has never been a country that resigns itself to the impossible—we have conquered countless diseases that once seemed unbeatable and transformed modern medicine for the world.  With that same spirit of discovery, compassion, and determination, we will keep searching for better treatments, earlier answers, and—one day—a cure for Alzheimer’s.

This month, we honor those fighting Alzheimer’s and the caregivers who stand beside them.  We remember those we have lost, embrace the families who carry their memories forward, and renew our promise to build an America where longer lives are also healthier lives. Together, we will Make America Healthy Again and give future generations the priceless gift of more years, more memories, and more time with the people they love.

America’s critical infrastructure is the foundation of our prosperity, the backbone of our national defense, and the bedrock of our resilience.  For more than two centuries, American workers, through their own ingenuity and grit, have built the infrastructure that enables the world’s greatest economy and strongest military.  During Critical Infrastructure Security and Resilience Month, we celebrate this long, rich legacy and reaffirm our commitment to expanding opportunity, fortifying our national security, and unleashing American innovation to keep our Nation free and resilient for generations to come.

My America First Resilience Strategy establishes a bold vision to secure such a future through commonsense transformation.  We are confronting the gravest threats to our homeland head-on to protect American lives, strengthen our communities, and safeguard livelihoods; upgrading our aging technology and infrastructure to guarantee dependable power, clean water, and modern communications for households nationwide while keeping our country ahead of its rivals; returning authority to the States and equipping governors, local leaders, and industries with the tools to prepare for and recover from any crisis; and streamlining government to deliver faster results and greater value for every hardworking citizen.  Our goal is clear:  to secure the supply chains and systems on which our Nation depends so that no adversary and no disaster will ever hold America or our core interests hostage.

For America to remain the champion of the world’s economy, our critical infrastructure must be built by American companies, supported by American workers, and secured against those who seek to exploit it.  Since returning to office, I have taken decisive action to reshore the manufacturing our critical infrastructure relies on.  To harness our abundant energy and natural resources, I declared a National Energy Emergency and signed an Executive Order on Unleashing American Energy, directing every Federal agency to expedite major energy projects.  I also established the National Energy Dominance Council, marshalling the full power of the Federal Government behind that vital mission, and invoked the Defense Production Act to strengthen domestic production of the transformers, transmission equipment, and other critical components essential to our electric grid and national defense.  Through this America First approach, we are expanding American oil, natural gas, and nuclear energy production and eliminating disastrous, unnecessary, or burdensome regulations to finally restore the reliable and affordable energy that powers the greatest Nation on Earth.

That America First commitment is more critical than ever as we enter a new era of digital infrastructure—the age of Super Intelligence (SI).  Across America, we are investing in SI data centers to power the American economy and ensure that we remain the global leader in this cutting-edge technology, especially as our adversaries compete against us for dominance.  Every new data center will unlock countless high-paying jobs in America’s SI industry.  Thanks to the work of my Administration, America’s largest technology companies have also signed the Ratepayer Protection Pledge, agreeing to pay for the new power generation and grid upgrades their data centers require instead of passing those costs on to American families.  As President, I will always stand up for the middle class and ensure that our companies put the American People first.

Our infrastructure is as strong as the Americans who build, operate, and defend it.  This Critical Infrastructure Security and Resilience Month, we honor the linemen, engineers, technicians, operators, cybersecurity professionals, and skilled workers whose dedication keeps America running.  Their unrivaled genius and determination represent the very best of our Nation, and together with them, we will build and maintain the infrastructure that makes America great.
